designationHistory.name: Stump Lake Reservation
designationHistory.indexText: President Theodore Roosevelt set aside four islands in Stump Lake, 27.39 acres, as the Stump Lake Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, by executive order on March 9, 1905.
designationHistory.note: Pass A (FWS Realty record: EO 296A, March 9, 1905, 27.39 acres) and Pass B (order text on Wikisource: four islands in T. 151 N., R. 61 W., total 27.39 acres, "to be known as the Stump Lake Reservation," dated March 9, 1905) agree. Signed by T.R. Renamed Stump Lake National Wildlife Refuge by Proclamation 2416, July 25, 1940. Wikisource is a transcription; a scan check against the original order or the GLO record would add a primary image.
